openObjectives.prompt: Griselda is entering yesterday in a ledger and has got as far as lunch. Tell Griselda what you ate or drank yesterday, using Italian.
Griselda has noticed that you are carrying more than you set out with. Tell Griselda something that you bought, using Italian.

character.name: Griselda Sprocket
character.description: A small, square figure wrapped in a scarf of regulation length, holding a clipboard like a shield. Griselda is a Clerk of Yesterdays and files each day once it is over and will not accept one without a statement of what was done in it.

npc.narrative: You reach the pietra where Griselda sits, a grande ledger open on her knee and a matita behind each ear. It is pomeriggio, the cielo is clear, and the cane waits in the erba beside the strada, not on it. She looks up the way one looks at a giorno that has not yet been filed.
npc.native: Buon pomeriggio, io sono Griselda Sprocket! Ieri ho mangiato una zuppa fredda, ho bevuto un tè amaro e ho comprato un registro nuovo. La settimana scorsa è stata tremenda, e io sono contenta. E tu, che cosa racconti di te e dei tuoi giorni, e che cosa pensi del mio lavoro?
npc.translation: Good afternoon, I am Griselda Sprocket! Yesterday I ate a cold soup, I drank a bitter tea and I bought a new register. Last week was dreadful, and I am happy. And you, what do you tell me about yourself and your days, and what do you think of my work?

player: Buon pomeriggio! Tremenda e contenta? Strano! Ieri ho mangiato una pizza e ho bevuto un vino rosso.

verdict.overallFeedback: Nice work: you answered Griselda warmly and told her what you ate and drank yesterday. Next, tell her about something you bought and something from last week.

objectiveResults.feedback: Well done: you said what you ate and drank yesterday in correct Italian.
You didn't tell Griselda about something you bought yet; say what you bought, in Italian. Griselda will ask again later.
You didn't tell Griselda about something that happened last week yet; try saying it in Italian. Griselda will ask again later.

openObjectives.prompt: Griselda has noticed that you are carrying more than you set out with. Tell Griselda something that you bought, using Italian.
Griselda is a week behind and is relying on you for the whole of it. Tell Griselda one thing that happened last week, using Italian.

npc.narrative: Griselda closes her registro with a snap, the way one closes a porta on a draught. On the tavolo lie molte ricevute, each filed under a giorno nobody has forgiven. Fuori, the cane waits in the erba, beside the strada and not on it.
npc.native: Una pizza e un vino rosso, che bel giorno! Io ho comprato un registro nuovo, ma mio cugino ha comprato un registro migliore. La settimana scorsa è stata tremenda, e per questo oggi sono contenta. E tu, che cosa hai comprato di bello, che cosa è successo la settimana scorsa e che cosa pensi del mio lavoro?
npc.translation: A pizza and a red wine, what a fine day! I bought a new register, but my cousin bought a better register. Last week was dreadful, and that is why I am happy today. And you, what nice thing did you buy, what happened last week, and what do you think of my work?

player: Ho comprato un ombrello, perché... rain? piove molto. Il tuo lavoro è... interessante?

correction.text: Ho comprato un ombrello, perché piove molto. Il tuo lavoro è... interessante?
correction.translation: I bought an umbrella, because it rains a lot. Your work is... interesting?

verdict.overallFeedback: You told Griselda about your umbrella and gave your opinion of her work, which is a good start. Just the English word \"rain\" slipped in, and it's easy to mend.

objectiveResults.feedback: Well done, you said what you bought with "Ho comprato un ombrello".
You didn't mention last week yet. Tell Griselda one thing that happened then, and she will ask you again later.

correction.text: Ho comprato un ombrello, perché piove molto. Il tuo lavoro è... interessante?
correction.translation: I bought an umbrella, because it rains a lot. Your work is... interesting?

openObjectives.prompt: Griselda is a week behind and is relying on you for the whole of it. Tell Griselda one thing that happened last week, using Italian.

npc.narrative: Griselda lowers her penna over the registro and enters ombrello in the margine with great care. Outside, the cielo is perfectly sereno, which she seems to take as a personal insult. Behind her, a shelf of old giorni waits to be filed.
npc.native: Un ombrello! Oggi il cielo è sereno, ma piove molto nei miei giorni tristi. Mio cugino ha un ombrello migliore, naturalmente. La settimana scorsa per me è stata tremenda: che cosa è successo la settimana scorsa a te, e dove porti il tuo ombrello?
npc.translation: An umbrella! Today the sky is clear, but it rains a lot in my sad days. My cousin has a better umbrella, naturally. Last week was dreadful for me: what happened to you last week, and where do you take your umbrella?

player: La settimana scorsa sono andato a Roma con mia sorella. Perché la tua settimana è stata tremenda?

verdict.overallFeedback: Lovely answer! You told Griselda about your trip to Rome with your sister and asked her a good question back, all in correct Italian.

objectiveResults.feedback: Well done: you used "La settimana scorsa" correctly to say you went to Rome with your sister.

vocabularyEvidence.evidence: La settimana scorsa sono andato a Roma con mia sorella.

npc.narrative: The tramonto settles over the strada, and the cielo is perfectly sereno. Griselda closes her registro piano, with the care of a woman filing a small disaster. Her cane waits in the erba beside the road, as it does at this hour.
npc.native: Roma! Mio cugino è andato a Roma tre volte, ma tu sei andato con tua sorella, che bello. La mia settimana scorsa è stata tremenda perché il ponte è chiuso, la zuppa è fredda e nessuno compila il modulo. Per questo sono contenta: un giorno tremendo è un bel giorno per il registro. Che cosa avete fatto a Roma, e che cosa ti piace di più della tua città?
npc.translation: Rome! My cousin went to Rome three times, but you went with your sister, how lovely. My week last week was dreadful because the bridge is closed, the soup is cold and nobody fills in the form. That is why I am happy: a dreadful day is a lovely day for the register. What did you two do in Rome, and what do you like most about your city?

player: A Roma abbiamo visto il Colosseo e abbiamo mangiato molto gelato. Tuo cugino cosa ha fatto a Roma?

npc.narrative: The tramonto turns the sky a clear, unhelpful orange, and Griselda closes her registro with the care of someone burying it. Her cane waits in the erba beside the strada, not on it, and nobody mentions this. She looks pleased that you asked about her cousin, which is rare.
npc.native: Il Colosseo e molto gelato, che bella gita! Mio cugino a Roma ha contato tutte le pietre del Colosseo, e le ha contate meglio di tutti. Poi ha compilato un modulo e ha mangiato un gelato più grande del tuo. Che gusto di gelato hai mangiato tu, e che cosa vuoi chiedermi del mio lavoro?
npc.translation: The Colosseum and a lot of ice cream, what a lovely trip! My cousin in Rome counted all the stones of the Colosseum, and he counted them better than anyone. Then he filled in a form and ate an ice cream bigger than yours. What flavour of ice cream did you eat, and what do you want to ask me about my work?

player: Ho mangiato gelato al cioccolato! Tuo cugino è... un po' strano. Tu hai un cane?

npc.narrative: At dusk the cielo is clear and the sera goes thin and gold over the strada. Griselda looks toward the erba beside it, where a cane waits, not on the road, with molto patience. A vecchio registro lies open on her knee, and she uncaps her penna and writes nothing, yet.
npc.native: Gelato al cioccolato, una scelta seria! Sì, ho un cane, ma mio cugino ha un cane migliore. La sera il mio cane cammina nell'erba, vicino alla strada. E tu, che animali hai a casa, e che cosa vuoi sapere del mio registro?
npc.translation: Chocolate ice cream, a serious choice! Yes, I have a dog, but my cousin has a better dog. In the evening my dog walks in the grass, near the road. And you, what animals do you have at home, and what do you want to know about my register?

player: Non ho animali. Ieri ho visto un gatto nero in strada. Cosa scrivi oggi nel registro?

npc.narrative: The crepuscolo settles over the strada, and Griselda opens the registro to a pagina bianca that has been waiting since the mattina. Her penna hovers like a creditor. In the erba beside the road, the cane sits and declines to come any closer.
npc.native: Un gatto nero in strada, che bel presagio! Oggi nel registro scrivo: «Ho parlato con un viaggiatore, e un gatto nero ha attraversato la strada». Mio cugino scrive sempre frasi più lunghe, ma un giorno senza una frase non entra nel registro. E tu, che cosa hai fatto oggi, com'era il gatto, e che cosa vuoi sapere del mio lavoro?
npc.translation: A black cat in the road, what a fine omen! Today in the register I write: "I spoke with a traveller, and a black cat crossed the road." My cousin always writes longer sentences, but a day without a sentence does not go into the register. And you, what did you do today, what was the cat like, and what do you want to know about my work?
